claims.text: The untreated W–Cu composite exhibits phase separation under the specified service conditions.
The untreated W–Cu composite develops interfacial voids under the specified service conditions.
A thin Ni coating can be deposited on the tungsten phase before final copper consolidation.
Pre-coating the tungsten phase with Ni produces a continuous interfacial layer bridging tungsten and copper.
The Ni interfacial layer improves wetting between tungsten and copper.
The Ni interfacial layer acts as an interdiffusion barrier between tungsten and copper.
The Ni layer reduces interfacial-energy mismatch between tungsten and copper.
Reducing interfacial-energy mismatch lowers the thermodynamic drive for phase separation.
The Ni layer reduces interfacial void formation under high-temperature and irradiation stresses.
Reduced phase separation and void formation improve the phase and interfacial stability of the composite.
The Ni-coated W–Cu composite will have higher effective thermal conductivity than the untreated composite under matched heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Interfacial void formation in the untreated composite lowers its thermal conductivity.
The intervention is applicable to particle-based and ligament-based W–Cu composites made by conventional sintering or infiltration.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity improvement may depend on Ni-layer thickness and uniformity.
